title: Creativity: Wallas, Guilford, 4C Model, Torrance, Investment Theory, Threshold Hypothesis
summary: Process of Creative Thinking (Wallas), Divergent Thinking (Guilford), 4C Model (Kaufman & Beghetto), 4P Model (Rhodes), Investment Theory (Sternberg & Lubart), Threshold Hypothesis (Guilford), Torrance Test of Creativity.
objectives: Describe Wallas' four stages of creative thinking.
Explain Sternberg and Lubart's Investment Theory.
Describe the Torrance Test of Creativity.
revision: Creativity: Wallas (Preparation→Incubation→Illumination→Verification). Guilford: divergent thinking. 4C Model: Mini-c→Little-c→Pro-c→Big-c. Investment Theory: buy low, sell high. Threshold: IQ ~120 necessary but not sufficient.
traps: Threshold Hypothesis: IQ ~120 is necessary but not sufficient for creativity.
TTCT measures fluency, flexibility, originality, elaboration.
confusions: Confusing divergent thinking (multiple answers) with convergent thinking (one answer).
Believing high IQ guarantees high creativity.

notes.t: Graham Wallas proposed four stages of creative thinking: Preparation, Incubation, Illumination, and Verification.
J.P. Guilford distinguished convergent thinking (single correct answer) from divergent thinking (multiple possible answers), a key component of creativity.
Kaufman and Beghetto proposed four levels: Mini-c (personal), Little-c (everyday), Pro-c (professional), and Big-c (eminent).
Mel Rhodes identified four Ps: Person, Process, Product, and Press (environment).
Sternberg and Lubart proposed that creativity is like investment: buying low (unknown ideas) and selling high (ideas that become valued).
Guilford proposed that intelligence is necessary for creativity up to a threshold (around IQ 120), beyond which more intelligence does not increase creativity.
The Torrance Test of Creative Thinking (TTCT) assesses creativity through verbal and figural tasks measuring fluency, flexibility, originality, and elaboration.
UGC NET frequently asks about Wallas' stages, Guilford's divergent thinking, Torrance's TTCT, and the Threshold Hypothesis.
